Currently, only 46% of close contacts are being monitored, and testing delays hinder containment efforts. The outbreak has also affected Uganda, which has reported 16 cases linked to travel from the DRC. Authorities emphasize the importance of safe burials to prevent transmission, while misinformation and community mistrust complicate the response. articleHeadline: Ebola in Democratic Republic of the Congo: Community resistance complicates outbreak response efforts
articleSummary: As of June 5, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has resulted in 389 confirmed cases and 63 deaths, primarily in Ituri province, linked to the Bundibugyo strain. Community resistance to hospitalization and safe burial practices complicates response efforts, with only 55.5% of identified contacts being monitored. The World Health Organization has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, emphasizing the urgent need for coordinated action. Recent violence against health workers has further hindered containment, as families often conduct burials independently, increasing transmission risks. Diagnostic capabilities have improved, with rapid PCR tests providing results within 24 hours. The outbreak has expanded, with over 1,000 suspected infections and more than 200 deaths reported. In a positive development, eight patients have recovered from the Bundibugyo strain. Regional health ministers are collaborating to standardize Ebola response efforts across DRC and Uganda, while Ghana activates its Ebola preparedness plan amid rising cases.

articleHeadline: Ebola in India: Monitoring and quarantine measures ramped up
articleSummary: As of June 4, 2026, India has intensified its Ebola monitoring protocols in response to rising infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda. Health authorities have implemented rigorous screening at airports, particularly targeting international travelers. A Sudanese man showing Ebola-like symptoms was isolated at Gandhi Hospital in Hyderabad after arriving at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, with test results pending. In Chhattisgarh, three individuals—two Indians and one Ugandan—are under a 21-day home quarantine after returning from Ebola-affected regions; they remain asymptomatic and are being monitored daily. Enhanced border screening and rapid response measures are actively in place to prevent potential outbreaks.
